# Alpha diversity of each time slice

The alpha diversity of the diatom community from each time slice was evaluated using Hill numbers (qD), as described by [Hill (1973)](https://doi.org/10.2307/1934352). We calculated the Hill numbers for q = 0, 1, and 2, which represent species richness (0D), Shannon diversity (1D), and Simpson diversity (2D), respectively. The order of q in Hill numbers affects how sensitive the index is to the relative abundance of species. Specifically, species richness (0D) treats all species equally, regardless of their abundance. In contrast, Shannon diversity (1D) emphasizes the number of equally abundant common species, while Simpson diversity (2D) focuses on the diversity of more abundant species [(Chao et al., 2014)](https://doi.org/10.1890/13-0133.1). 

Shannon diversity (order q = 1) is often regarded as an optimal measure because it balances between species richness (q = 0) and Simpson diversity. Higher-order Hill numbers (q > 1) may be overly sensitive to both rare and dominant species [(Roswell et al., 2021)](https://doi.org/10.1111/oik.07202). Therefore, for simplicity, we may choose to use only species richness (0D) and Shannon diversity (1D).

The observed diversity is influenced by sample completeness [(Chao et al., 2020)](https://doi.org/10.1111/1440-1703.12102). To address this, we either rarefied or extrapolated the estimated Hill numbers using the R package iNEXT (Chao et al., 2014). This process involved bootstrap resampling 1,000 times to produce a smooth mean diversity accumulation curve, complete with a 95% confidence interval across various levels of sample completeness [(Chao et al., 2020)](https://doi.org/10.1111/1440-1703.12102). We established a sample completeness threshold of 90%, which represents the minimum value of maximum sample completeness for over 97% of the samples. This approach standardizes sampling efforts and ensures a fair estimation of alpha diversity [(Chao & Ricotta, 2019)](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.2852). 

Additionally, we calculated ratios of estimated Shannon diversity and Simpson diversity to species richness, denoted as 1E = 1D/0D and 2E = 2D/0D, to serve as evenness indices. These ratios reflect the effective proportions of equally abundant common and dominant species within the community [(Chao & Ricotta, 2019)](https://doi.org/10.1002/ecy.2852). For simplicity, we will focus mainly on the results of 1E.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(iNEXT)

sample <- apply(spp[!zero,], 1, function(x) sort(x[x!=0], decreasing = TRUE))

# Function for abundance-based iNterpolation and EXTrapolation of Hill number
iNEXT_fun <-
  function(x, ...){
    q0 <- iNEXT(x, q=0, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    q0.25 <- iNEXT(x, q=0.25, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    q0.5 <- iNEXT(x, q=0.5, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    q0.75 <- iNEXT(x, q=0.75, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    q1 <- iNEXT(x, q=1, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    q1.25 <- iNEXT(x, q=1.25, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    q1.5 <- iNEXT(x, q=1.5, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    q1.75 <- iNEXT(x, q=1.75, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    q2 <- iNEXT(x, q=2, datatype = "abundance", ...)
    out1 <- q0$DataInfo
    out2 <- rbind(q0$iNextEst$size_based,q0.25$iNextEst$size_based, q0.5$iNextEst$size_based,
                  q0.75$iNextEst$size_based, q1$iNextEst$size_based,q1.25$iNextEst$size_based,
                  q1.5$iNextEst$size_based, q1.75$iNextEst$size_based,q2$iNextEst$size_based)
    out3 <- rbind(q0$iNextEst$coverage_based,q0.25$iNextEst$coverage_based, 
                  q0.5$iNextEst$coverage_based, q0.75$iNextEst$coverage_based,
                  q1$iNextEst$coverage_based,q1.25$iNextEst$coverage_based,
                  q1.5$iNextEst$coverage_based, q1.75$iNextEst$coverage_based,
                  q2$iNextEst$coverage_based)
    out4 <- q0$AsyEst
    out <- list(out1, out2, out3, out4)
    names(out) <- c("DataInfo", "iNextEst_size_based", "iNextEst_coverage_based", "AsyEst")
    return(out)
  }

library(foreach)
library(doSNOW)

cl<-makeCluster(16) # change the 16 to your number of CPU cores
registerDoSNOW(cl) # register the SNOW parallel backend with the foreach package
sample_h <- foreach(i=1:length(sample), .packages="iNEXT") %dopar% iNEXT_fun(sample[[i]], knots=100, se=TRUE, nboot=1000)
stopCluster(cl) # stop a SNOW cluster
names(sample_h) <- names(sample)
save(sample_h, file="../Rdata/sample_h1.rda")
```

# Diversity accumulation curves

## Size-based curves

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
load("../Rdata/sample_h1.rda")

hs <- ldply(lapply(sample_h, FUN=function(x)x$iNextEst_size_based), .id="Sample")
hc <- ldply(lapply(sample_h, FUN=function(x)x$iNextEst_coverage_based), .id="Sample")

ggplot()+
  geom_line(data= subset(hs, Method!="Observed"), 
            aes(x=m, y=qD, colour=Method, group=Sample))+
  geom_point(data= subset(hs, Method=="Observed"), 
            aes(x=m, y=qD, group=Sample))+
  facet_wrap(~Order.q, scale="free")+
  labs(x = "Numbers of Individuals", y = expression(Hill~Number~(italic(""^q*D))),
       colour="Method")+
  theme_bw()%+replace% large #%+replace% no_strip
```

Fig. X. Size-based diversity accumulation curves for each time slice. The blue lines indicate the interpolated (rarefied) and red lines indicate extrapolated parts of the accumulation curves based on 1000 permutations. Dotted symbols indicate the observed diversity values.

## Coverage-based curves

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
ggplot()+
  geom_line(data= subset(hc, Method!="Observed"), 
            aes(x=m, y=SC, colour=Method, group=Sample))+
  geom_point(data= subset(hc, Method=="Observed"), 
            aes(x=m, y=SC, group=Sample))+
  facet_wrap(~Order.q, scale="free")+
  labs(x = "Numbers of Individuals", y = "Sample Coverage",
       colour="Method")+
  theme_bw()%+replace% large #%+replace% no_strip
```

Fig. X. Sample coverage accumulation curves for each time slice. The blue lines indicate the interpolated (rarefied) and red lines indicate extrapolated parts of the accumulation curves based on 1000 permutations. Dotted symbols indicate the observed diversity values.

# Maxiumum diversity from accumulation curves

## Maximum sample coverage 

```{r, eval=FALSE}
a <- lapply(sample_h, FUN=function(x)x$iNextEst_size_based)%>%ldply(.id="Sample")
a <- lapply(splitBy(~Sample+Order.q, a, omit = FALSE), FUN=function(x)x[dim(x)[1],]) %>% ldply
a <- cbind(sam[match(a$Sample, sam$Age_ka),], a[, -1:-2])
save(a, file="../Rdata/hillmax.rda")
```

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
load("../Rdata/hillmax.rda")
ggplot(data= a, aes(x=Order.q, y=SC, colour=Period2, group=Age_ka))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_point()+
  facet_wrap(~Period2)+
  labs(x = "Order q", y = "Sample Coverage",
       colour="Period")+
  theme_bw()%+replace% large #%+replace% no_strip
```

Fig. X. The maximum sample coverage in each time slice as a function of order q. There are roughly 97% of time slices having maximum sample coverage below 90%. We set 90% sample coverage as threshold to standardize Hill numbers; however, this approach likely underestimate the alpha diversity in these ~3% of samples. 

## Hill number profiles

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(data= a, aes(x=Order.q, y=qD, colour=Period2, group=Age_ka))+
  geom_line(size=1)+
  geom_point()+
  facet_wrap(~Period2)+
  labs(x = "Order q", y = expression(Hill~Number~(italic(""^q*D))),
       colour="Period")+
  theme_bw()%+replace% large #%+replace% no_strip
```

Fig. X. Hill number profile of each time slice based on maximum sample coverage. The overall elevation of the profile indicates the diversity based on hill number across different order q. The levelness of the line indicates species evenness of the assemblage, because a complete leveled diversity profile would suggest that the numbers of total, common and dominant species are all the same.

Fig. X. Coverage-based Diversity accumulation curves. The blue lines indicate the interpolated (rarefied) and red lines indicate extrapolated parts of the accumulation curves based on 1000 permutations. Dotted symbols indicate the observed diversity values. Because not all accumulation curves have reached asymptotic, we choose the Sample Coverage = 90% to standardize the Hill number estimates.

# Normalized slope of Hill number profile (species evenness)

```{r}
# Alpha diversity for each time slice
# Hill numbers of order q = 0, 1, 2
d0 <- subset(hc2, Order.q==0)
d1 <- subset(hc2, Order.q==1)
d2 <- subset(hc2, Order.q==2)
# Species evenness based on normalized slope of Hill number profile (Jost, 2010, Chao & Ricotta, 2019, Table 1)
e1 <- (d1$qD-1)/(d0$qD-1)
e2 <- (d2$qD-1)/(d0$qD-1)

div <- cbind(d0=d0$qD, d1=d1$qD, d2=d2$qD, e1, e2) %>% as.data.frame
div <-cbind(sam, div[match(sam$Age_ka, d0$Age_ka),])
div[zero, c("d0", "d1", "d2")] <- 0
```

# Combine alpha & species evenness

```{r}
div_m <- melt(div, id.vars = names(sam)[-13], measure.vars = c("logDAR", "d0", "d1", "d2", "e1", "e2"))

div_m$label <- factor(div_m$variable, labels= c(expression(log[10]("DAR")), expression(""^0*italic(D)), expression(""^1*italic(D)), expression(""^2*italic(D)), expression(""^1*E), expression(""^2*E)))

div_m <- div_m[!is.na(div_m$value),]

save(div, file="../Rdata/div.rda")
write.csv(div, file = "../Data/20220419_MD012414_diatom_all_with_ancillary_data.csv")
```

# Descriptive statistics by MIS stages

```{r}
# Top x-axis
ax2 <- subset(mis, Period=="Interglacial")

# Descriptive statistics of each panel
out <- summaryBy(value~variable+MIS, FUN=function(x)c(mean(x, na.rm=T), sd(x, na.rm=T), se(x, na.rm=T), length(x)), div_m)
names(out)[-1:-2] <- c("value.mean", "value.sd", "value.se", "value.length")
out <- cbind(out, mis[match(out$MIS, mis$MIS), -1:-2])
out$label <- factor(out$variable, labels= c(expression(log[10]("DAR")), expression(""^0*italic(D)), expression(""^1*italic(D)), expression(""^2*italic(D)), expression(""^1*E), expression(""^2*E)))

# Minimum and maximum ranges of each panel
ci_range <- cbind(variable= out$variable, with(out, cbind(value.mean-value.se*1.96, value.mean+value.se*1.96)) %>% as.data.frame) %>% melt(id.var="variable", variable.name="range") # min and max values of 95% CI 
p_range <- rbind(ci_range[,-2], div_m[, c("variable", "value")]) # combine 95% CI with the Hill numbers

ax3 <- lapply(splitBy(~variable, p_range, omit = FALSE), FUN=function(x)cbind(ax2, ymin=min(x$value, na.rm=T), ymax=max(x$value, na.rm=T))) %>% ldply(.id="variable")

ax3$label <- factor(ax3$variable, 
                    levels=c("logDAR", "d0", "d1", "d2", "e1","e2"), 
                    labels= c(expression(log[10]("DAR")), expression(""^0*italic(D)), expression(""^1*italic(D)), expression(""^2*italic(D)), expression(""^1*E), expression(""^2*E)))

# Mid-Pleistocene Transition
mpt <- c(Start=830, End=1230) %>% as.data.frame %>% t
mpt <- lapply(splitBy(~variable, p_range, omit = FALSE), FUN=function(x)cbind(mpt, ymin=min(x$value, na.rm=T), ymax=max(x$value, na.rm=T))) %>% ldply(.id="variable")
mpt$label <- factor(mpt$variable, 
                    levels=c("logDAR", "d0", "d1", "d2", "e1","e2"), 
                    labels= c(expression(log[10]("DAR")), expression(""^0*italic(D)), expression(""^1*italic(D)), expression(""^2*italic(D)), expression(""^1*E), expression(""^2*E)))
```

# Temporal variation of alpha diversity
* Oblique striped area shows Mid-Pleistocene Transition
* Hill numbers of order q = 0, 1, 2
* Species evenness of order q = 1, 2

```{r, fig.height=20, fig.width=15}
ax2b <- ax2[(1:dim(ax2)[1]) %% 2 != 0,]
ggplot()+
  geom_rect_pattern(data=mpt, aes(xmin=Start, xmax=End, ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax), pattern="stripe", pattern_alpha = 0.1, fill="transparent", pattern_density = 0.3, colour="black", linetype = 4)+
  geom_rect(data=ax3, aes(xmin=Start, xmax=End, ymin=ymin, ymax=ymax), fill="gray", colour="transparent", alpha=0.2)+
  geom_rect(data=subset(out, value.length>2), aes(xmin=Start, xmax=End, ymin=value.mean-value.se*1.96, ymax=value.mean+value.se*1.96, fill=Period), alpha=0.6)+
  geom_segment(data=out, aes(x=Start, y=value.mean, xend=End, yend=value.mean, color=Period), alpha=1, size=1)+
  #geom_point(data=div_m, aes(x=Age_ka, y=value), size=0.5)+
  geom_line(data=div_m, aes(x=Age_ka, y=value))+
  #stat_smooth(data=div_m, aes(x=Age_ka, y=value), method="gam", formula=y~s(x))+
  labs(x = "Age (ka)", y = expression("Diatom accumulation rate"~(valves~cm^-2~y^-1)~"and"~alpha-"diversity"))+
  scale_fill_viridis_d(direction = -1)+
  scale_colour_viridis_d(direction = -1)+
  scale_x_reverse(expand=expansion(mult = 0.01), breaks=seq(0, 1550, 100), sec.axis = sec_axis(~.*1, breaks = with(ax2b, (Start+End)/2), labels = ax2b$MIS))+
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.01))+
  facet_wrap(~label, labeller = label_parsed, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", strip.position="right")+
  theme_bw()%+replace% large2 %+replace% vert_x  %+replace% theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Fig. X. Temporal variations of diatom accumulation rate (DAR), Hill numbers (order q = 0, 1, 2) and species evenness (order q = 1, 2). The missing values of Hill numbers (order q = 0, 1, 2) are set to zero diversity (i.e., no specimen). The missing values of species evenness (order q = 0, 1, 2) are omitted due to zero Hill numbers. The oblique striped area shows Mid-Pleistocene Transition (MPT).

* Ratio of Simpson diversity to species richness 

```{r, fig.height=12, fig.width=12}
ggplot(data=pair, aes(x=value, y=e2, colour=Period))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x = "Ancillary variables", y = expression("Species evenness"~(""^2*E)))+
  facet_wrap(~variable, labeller = label_parsed, scales = "free", ncol=6)+
  theme_bw()%+replace% large %+replace% vert_x

ggplot(data=pair, aes(x=value, y=e2, colour=Period2))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(x = "Ancillary variables", y = expression("Species evenness"~(""^2*E)))+
  facet_wrap(~variable, labeller = label_parsed, scales = "free", ncol=6)+
  theme_bw()%+replace% large %+replace% vert_x
```
